svg.title: Figure 3. Three-dimensional Mohr's circles at H
svg.desc: Two sets of three Mohr's circles for point H, without numbers. In each, the solid circle is the in-plane circle through A and B, and the two dashed circles join A and B to the origin O, which represents the zero radial stress at the free surface. (a) Lever load only: A is tensile and B is slightly compressive, so the origin lies inside the in-plane circle and the in-plane maximum shear is also the absolute maximum. (b) With internal pressure added: both A and B are tensile, the origin lies outside the in-plane circle, and the largest circle runs from O to A; the absolute maximum shear (its radius, sigma max over 2) is about one and a half times the in-plane value.
